hook.line: Vale's mother has a few facts wrong about the new café owner. A bare *no* just starts an argument; a correction says what's wrong and then what's right.
hook.es: No, no es de Estados Unidos, es de Canadá.
hook.en: No, he's not from the United States, he's from Canada.

rule:
A correction has two moves: deny the wrong fact, then give the right one. *No, no es de Cali, es de Medellín.* The first *no* answers them; the second belongs to the verb.

If someone says something negative that isn't true, flip it with *sí*: *No hablas inglés, ¿no? Sí, sí hablo.* English says yes, I do; Spanish repeats the real verb: *sí hablo*, *sí tengo*.

A bare *no* isn't a correction. Add the fact.
smallPrint: The doubled *sí, sí* is emphasis, like stressing I DO in English. Careful: a doubled *no, no* can also agree with a negative (*No es difícil. No, no es difícil.*); what came before tells you which.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *Tomás es de Estados Unidos.* Choose *Sí* or *No* to start, then fix it: ___, no es de Estados Unidos, es de Canadá. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: No, no es de Estados Unidos, es de Canadá.
yourTurn.why: They said something wrong, so you start with *no* and then give the right country.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *No hablas español, ¿no?* You do. Choose *Sí, sí hablo* or *No, no hablo* and type it.
yourTurn.why: To contradict a negative, use *sí* and repeat the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *Hernando es periodista.* Correct them: no, he's not a journalist, he's a taxi driver.
yourTurn.answer: No, no es periodista, es taxista.
yourTurn.why: Deny the wrong job, then give the right one.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *Vale es de Cali.* Correct them: she's from Medellín.
yourTurn.answer: No, no es de Cali, es de Medellín.
yourTurn.why: The second *no* goes right before *es*; then the right city.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone asks you (a man) *¿Eres el novio de Vale?* You're not; you're her friend. Correct them.
yourTurn.answer: No, no soy el novio de Vale, soy su amigo.
accept: No, no soy su novio, soy su amigo.
yourTurn.why: Same two moves, about you: *no soy*, then *soy*.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *No tienes hermanos, ¿no?* You have a sister. Contradict them, then add the fact.
yourTurn.answer: Sí, sí tengo. Tengo una hermana.
yourTurn.why: *Sí* flips their negative; then say what you have.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone says *El examen es el lunes.* It's on Tuesday. Correct them.
yourTurn.answer: No, no es el lunes, es el martes.
yourTurn.why: Deny the wrong day, then give the right one.

pitfalls.right: No, no es de Cali, es de Medellín.
pitfalls.why: A bare *no* leaves them guessing. Add the right fact.
To *No hablas español, ¿no?*, English says yes, I do. Spanish repeats the real verb: *sí hablo*.

pitfalls.wrong: No, es no de Cali, es de Medellín.
pitfalls.right: No, no es de Cali, es de Medellín.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *No* always goes before the verb: *no es*, never *es no*.

personal: Think of something people often get wrong about you: where you're from, your job, even your name. Write the correction: *No, no soy…, soy…*
